Population: all patients who had both valid baseline and final, after deduplication. The code deduplicated, excluded baseline -999, corrected batch B, and computed change for all remaining rows. But they didn't filter for missing final; they assume all have final (since they didn't check for missing final). The dataset has no nulls in biomarker_final per description (nulls 0). So okay. So scope matches.

Units: ng/mL. They corrected batch B dividing by 10, assuming original was µg/L (10x). That matches premise. So scope okay.

They didn't discuss that duplicate patients may have different baseline/final values; they kept highest sample_seq, which is per premise. So no major ignored problem.

One possible issue: they didn't verify that after correction, any biomarker_final values become unrealistic (e.g., negative). Not shown. But not required.

5. FALSE PREMISE: The premises are all true per data. They assumed batch B values are 10x too large; that's premise. So fine.
